task: T22 joint parity/chirality operation interface only

scope.reviewed: frozen 4.5 lines 5, 81–99; accepted 3.7 operation conventions; primary sources at specified locators
scope.not_reviewed: whole section, full dissertation, experimental-pattern certification, errata search, general RAT-PRM models

verdict.father_hypothesis: correct for the stated active rotation and beta30-only model: P flips beta30 but leaves axial vectors and chi invariant; C flips both beta30 and chi; PC preserves beta30 and flips chi
verdict.qualification: Whether C or PC is a symmetry of a particular intrinsic or full Hamiltonian depends on its degrees of freedom, constraints, external time-odd fields and implementation; this transformation table alone does not prove symmetry, state independence, energy degeneracy or a physical quartet. Under a passive reorientation of body axes every component and label must transform consistently.

conventions.axes: fixed right-handed principal axes x=1, y=2, z=3; Q diagonal with distinct eigenvalues; only beta30 Y30 is present; all changes are active at fixed oriented axes
conventions.angular_symbols: a denotes each of jp, jn, R; entries list the three components of the axial vector
conventions.chi: jp dot (jn cross R), parity-even and time-odd; axial triple product is not generally a spatial-parity-odd pseudoscalar
conventions.parity_phase: eta labels the sign of a shape coefficient in this oriented frame; it is neither a laboratory parity eigenvalue nor the arbitrary quantum-state phase produced by an operation
conventions.gauge: reversing the oriented principal axes by a proper D2 rotation changes the beta30 coordinate sign; distinguish labels from physical shapes and transform angular momenta at the same time

quantum_algebra.commutators: [P,T]=[P,Ry(pi)]=[P,C]=0 and T commutes with rotations, with antiunitary composition handled correctly
quantum_algebra.antiunitary_limit: antiunitary eigenphases change under state rephasing; (1±C)/2 is not a complex-linear projection. Ordinary parity projectors are (1±P)/2; nonzero projected norm and rank require checking.

locators: PDF pp. 9–11 Figs. 3–4 and angular momentum RMS discussion
findings: Full formal potential includes beta30, beta31, beta32, beta33 and induced dipoles; reported beta3=0.02 cannot be silently identified as a complete published beta3mu specification solely from the inspected passages.

Core parity splitting appears in Eq. (2); PDF p.5 defines P-hat as core parity, p-hat as total parity, and S2=P-hat R2 as reflection through the plane perpendicular to 2; Eqs. (14)–(15) construct good-total-parity intrinsic wavefunctions, Eq. (13) symmetrizes the strong-coupling basis.

S2 as written in that factorized core formulation must not automatically be equated with total P Ry(pi) or PC; establish the operators on the complete Hilbert space before doing so. The paper calls S2 a reflection operator; treating it as simplex terminology is interpretive.
Inspected formalism does not explicitly define C=T Ry(pi) or assert that C preserves the sign of beta30; pp.9–11 infer geometry from root-mean-square angular-momentum components, not signed chi.
In the paper’s numerical axis convention axis 1 is intermediate, 2 short, 3 long (PDF p.9); our fixed y=2 should not be asserted to be its intermediate axis.
PDF p.13 notes a different negative-parity dominant configuration in the RAT-PRM relative to the earlier TPRM; this does not by itself prove absence of a common reflection-asymmetric intrinsic space.

findings: Experimental and model context is the multiple chiral doublet and octupole-correlation interpretation; the present task does not re-audit all measured transitions or certify a static quartet.
Accepted convention C=T Ry(pi), chi parity even/time odd, C²=+1 and absence of a linear antiunitary parity projector remain intact. The conditional PC bridge refines the map without redefining C.

nonuniversal_harmonic_control.real_harmonics: z(2z²−3x²−3y²) is proportional to r³Y30 and reverses under Ry(pi); y(4z²−x²−y²) is a real sine-type rank-3 m=1 component and is invariant under the same rotation. Both reverse under P.
nonuniversal_harmonic_control.scope: second harmonic shows why no common sign can be assigned to arbitrary beta3mu; it need not belong to Wang’s selected reflection-symmetric ansatz

finite_validation.scope: independent small matrices: parity two-level shape and three distinguishable spins j=1/2 or 1; tests all rows, antiunitary operations, squares and commutation, plus real harmonic example. It is not a RAT-PRM prediction or a norm-kernel rank calculation.

known_limits: No source errata audit; no textbook primary-page inspection; no claim that Wang explicitly uses the C/PC interface above.
No proof that four named wave packets are independent or that any projected low-energy bands exist; no numerical norm-kernel or full nuclear Hamiltonian was computed.
The presence of arbitrary octupole modes or time-odd external constraints requires repeating the symmetry analysis.
C²=+1 alone supplies no Kramers degeneracy, but other independent symmetries or accidents can still generate degeneracies.
